annotations.title: Check a map's parts against known alleles

description: Compare each recognised part in a GenBank record — resistance markers, origins, promoters, terminators, reporters, tags — with the alleles of that part in a bundled library of public vectors. Every recognised feature is classed as matching the most common allele, matching another known allele (with the number of the library's vectors that carry those exact bases), an unseen variant (every difference listed with its position and bases, flagged critical for a marker, origin, promoter or coding sequence and minor otherwise), or not recognised. Parts are recognised by their bases first and their label second, a feature is compared as a window of the part (depositors draw the same origin at different spans) except a gene, which must reach its own start and stop, and a label that names one part over another's bases is reported. The reference is the most common allele in the bundled library of N vectors and nothing more: a depositor's error in one record is in the table, and matching a known allele says nothing about whether a part works.

text.description: A GenBank record (LOCUS … FEATURES … ORIGIN … //) or an EMBL/ENA one, at most 1,000,000 bases. A multi-record file is read from its first record.
